\chapter{Sign Up at Reception}
\label{ch:apuntarse-recepcion}
\hlchaptermodality{414}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can understand where and when to sign up for a class.}

Retrieve sign up and reception in a simple class notice.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[apuntarse]{apuntarse — put your name on the list}

\label{lesson:ES-C414-apuntarse}



\begin{quote}
Recall \textbf{el punto}, a point or item. Spanish builds \textbf{apuntar} from that family, and \textbf{apuntarse} can mean to put your own name down: to sign up.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
The base \textbf{punto} goes back to Latin \textbf{punctum}, a mark made by a prick. To \textbf{apuntar} is to note or point something; with \textbf{se}, \textbf{apuntarse} often means to add oneself to a list. The root is already anchored in \textbf{punto}, so this lesson extends that family.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: who signs up?}]
The pronoun changes with the person: \textbf{me apunto} for “I sign up” and \textbf{apuntarse} after another verb, as in \textbf{hay que apuntarse}, “one must sign up.” Use \textbf{a} for the activity: \textbf{apuntarse a una clase}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{apuntarse}
  \item \emph{me apunto a la clase}
  \item \emph{hay que apuntarse antes}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To sign up? (\emph{Apuntarse}.) One must sign up beforehand? (\emph{Hay que apuntarse antes}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/apuntar}{DLE: apuntar}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la recepción]{la recepción — the place that receives you}

\label{lesson:ES-C414-recepcion}



\begin{quote}
Recall \textbf{apuntarse}, to put your name on a list. At a sports centre, the list may be kept at \textbf{la recepción}, the reception desk.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
Latin \textbf{receptio} meant a receiving. Spanish \textbf{recepción} and English \textbf{reception} belong to the same family. The place receives visitors, questions and sign-up requests.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: place after en}]
Use \textbf{en la recepción} for “at the reception desk.” The written accent marks the final stress: re-cep-\textbf{CIÓN}. A useful notice says \textbf{Hay que apuntarse en la recepción}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{la recepción}
  \item \emph{en la recepción}
  \item \emph{hay que apuntarse en la recepción}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Reception desk? (\emph{La recepción}.) At reception? (\emph{En la recepción}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/recepci\%C3\%B3n}{DLE: recepción}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{sign-up recall one — action and place}

\label{lesson:ES-C414-signup-recall-1}



\begin{quote}
Give the action and the place. (\emph{Apuntarse, recepción}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{en la recepción}
  \item \emph{hay que apuntarse en la recepción}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sign up, reception? (\emph{Apuntarse, recepción}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{sign-up recall two — read the class notice}

\label{lesson:ES-C414-signup-recall-2}



\begin{quote}
A yoga class has limited places. The notice tells visitors what to do before class and where to do it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item “One must sign up beforehand.” {[}YOU SAY: \emph{Hay que apuntarse antes.}{]}
  \item “One must sign up at reception.” {[}YOU SAY: \emph{Hay que apuntarse en la recepción.}{]}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What must a visitor do before the class? (\emph{Apuntarse en la recepción}.)
